chunks: Three [narrators] — Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from Abu Malik al-Hadhrami, from Muhammad ibn Abul Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Uthman, from Aslam al-Mekki, from Abut-Tufayl, from Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, who said:

A caliph will be killed, for whom there is no intercessor in the Heaven, nor a supporter on the earth, and another caliph will be deposed until he walks on the face of the earth having nothing from the earth, and the son of the bondmaid will become the caliph.
He said: Then Abu-Tufayl said: O my nephew, I wish that I and you were from his time.
I said: And why do you wish for that, O uncle?
He said: Because Hudhayfa has told me that the rule will return to the Prophet's family.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of political change before the appearance of the Mahdi according to Hudhayfa?
ai.summary: This narration from Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, transmitted through the chain of al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, highlights the transitional political chaos preceding the Mahdi's appearance, characterized by the failure of existing caliphates and the eventual restoration of authority to the Ahl al-Bayt. Abu-Tufayl’s longing for that era underscores the Shia belief that true sovereignty (MulK) returns to the Prophet's lineage, fulfilling the promise of divine justice after a period of widespread corruption.
